title: GPU memory capacity slicing & dynamic buffer corridor for weights/KV/activations
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Goal: introduce a deterministic GPU memory partitioning and adaptive buffer corridor that slices device memory into three pragmatic compartments (weights, KV cache, activations) and provides an automated controller that adjusts slice ratios based on recent runtime signals. This ticket designs the model for capacity slicing, implements the controller prototype, integrates a preflight occupancy sensor into the serving agent, and validates behaviour via the simulation harness and canary pool. The approach favors predictable tail-latency behavior for multi-tenant inference while improving utilization compared to fixed static reservations.
acceptance_criteria: A deterministic slicing algorithm that maps configured slice ratios to device offsets and enforces them in the runtime allocator
A rolling-window estimator that suggests slice ratio adjustments from live metrics (batch-length percentiles, kv-hit ratio, activation peak samples)
Preflight occupancy sensor in the request path that rejects or routes requests when a predicted activation spike would violate the buffer corridor
Simulation harness demonstrates >=8% increase in average GPU utilization on mixed workloads with <=5% regression in P99 latency
Canary rollout plan and feature flag gating are implemented and documented
Telemetry: per-slice peak/median occupancy, cross-slice spills, eviction counts, and routing rejections are emitted and visualized in the console
implementation_plan: 1) Design memory map: partition device memory into WeightRegion (static), CacheRegion (KV, variable), EphemeralRegion (activations). 2) Implement allocator enforcement: runtime enforces high-water and soft-water marks per region; evictions only permitted from CacheRegion subject to policy. 3) Build adaptive controller: periodic job computes recommended ratios using percentile-based heuristics and a smoothing window; recommendations are advisory by default and auto-apply in canary. 4) Add preflight sensor: for each incoming batch, simulate activation increment based on model profile and batch tokens; if predicted EphemeralRegion exceed soft limit, route to fallback model/queue. 5) Integrate metrics and dashboards, add feature flags and rollout gating. 6) Run simulation matrix (short/long sequences, many small requests, KV-heavy conversational) and tune smoothing and safety multiplier.
test_plan:
- Unit tests for allocator enforcement and region boundary conditions.
- Integration test: inject synthetic activation peaks and validate eviction and routing decisions.
- Simulation: replay real production request traces (anonymized) through the simulator to evaluate utilization/latency trade-offs.
- Canary: roll to 5 dedicated GPUs in us-west-2 with detailed telemetry and automatic rollback on QoS violations.
- Chaos test: force KV-store eviction failures and confirm graceful routing/fallback.
- CI perf job: nightly run comparing baseline and new controller over standard benchmark suite.

2026-03-09 — Marco Ortega: Added preflight occupancy estimator; basic model profiles bundled for gpt-3.5-like and chat-xl. Need to expand model profiles and validate estimation accuracy against KV-enabled runs.

notes: Trade-offs: stricter enforcement reduces tail-risk but can under-utilize memory for bursty KV-heavy tenants. We intentionally prioritize predictable tail latency for paid tiers and provide a tuning path for best-effort tiers. Consider integrating quantization-informed weight shrinkage to reclaim static footprint in future work. Also evaluate alignment with Dedicated capacity billing implications.
next_steps: 1) Complete async eviction implementation (Marco) 2) Expand model profiles to cover 6 commonly served architectures (Aisha) 3) Draft canary runbook and attach to PR (Priya) 4) Schedule architecture sync to finalize auto-apply policy (Anthony)
implementation_risks:
- Fragmentation within EphemeralRegion leading to inability to pack activations efficiently.
- Eviction storms if KV churn is higher than forecast.
- Incorrect estimator biases causing unnecessary routing rejections.
- Accounting and billing misalignment for Dedicated customers if memory slices are enforced differently.
canary_plan: Phase 1: 5 GPUs in us-west-2 for 48 hours (low-traffic window); Phase 2: 20 GPUs with 7-day observation; Automatic rollback on sustained P99 increase >10% or routing_rejections >50/min
communication_plan: Notify customers in dedicated beta cohort 48 hours before canary via email and console banner; add docs explaining behavior and tuning knobs.
